back_blocks.md: A polymer is a large molecule built up from many smaller molecules called **monomers**, each joined to the next by covalent bonds.

cards.back_md: A polymer is a large molecule built up from many smaller molecules called **monomers**, each joined to the next by covalent bonds.

front_blocks.md: In addition polymerisation of ethene, the C=C **..........** bond in each monomer breaks so the monomers can join together.

back_blocks.md: In addition polymerisation of ethene, the C=C **double** bond in each monomer breaks so the monomers can join together.

cards.front_md: In addition polymerisation of ethene, the C=C **..........** bond in each monomer breaks so the monomers can join together.
cards.back_md: In addition polymerisation of ethene, the C=C **double** bond in each monomer breaks so the monomers can join together.

front_blocks.md: Addition polymerisation of ethene produces poly(ethene) and water.

back_blocks.md: Addition polymerisation produces **only one product, poly(ethene)**. No other molecules are released during the reaction.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Addition polymerisation of ethene produces poly(ethene) and water.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Addition polymerisation produces **only one product, poly(ethene)**. No other molecules are released during the reaction.

front_blocks.md: What monomer is used to make poly(ethene)?

back_blocks.md: Poly(ethene) is made from **ethene** monomers. Many ethene molecules join together in addition polymerisation to form the long-chain polymer.

cards.front_md: What monomer is used to make poly(ethene)?
cards.back_md: Poly(ethene) is made from **ethene** monomers. Many ethene molecules join together in addition polymerisation to form the long-chain polymer.

front_blocks.md: Poly(ethene), PVC and nylon are all examples of **..........** .

back_blocks.md: Poly(ethene), PVC and nylon are all examples of **polymers**.

cards.front_md: Poly(ethene), PVC and nylon are all examples of **..........** .
cards.back_md: Poly(ethene), PVC and nylon are all examples of **polymers**.

front_blocks.md: Why must an alkene, rather than an alkane, be used as a monomer for addition polymerisation?

back_blocks.md: An alkene must be used because addition polymerisation requires the **C=C double bond** to break and form new bonds with adjacent monomers. Alkanes have only single bonds and cannot do this.

cards.front_md: Why must an alkene, rather than an alkane, be used as a monomer for addition polymerisation?
cards.back_md: An alkene must be used because addition polymerisation requires the **C=C double bond** to break and form new bonds with adjacent monomers. Alkanes have only single bonds and cannot do this.

back_blocks.md: Condensation polymerisation is a process in which two different **monomers** link together repeatedly with the removal of a small molecule (usually **water**) to form a polymer.

cards.back_md: Condensation polymerisation is a process in which two different **monomers** link together repeatedly with the removal of a small molecule (usually **water**) to form a polymer.

front_blocks.md: In addition polymerisation, **..........** product is formed, whereas in condensation polymerisation a **..........** molecule is also produced at each linkage.

back_blocks.md: In addition polymerisation, **one** product is formed, whereas in condensation polymerisation a **water** molecule is also produced at each linkage.

cards.front_md: In addition polymerisation, **..........** product is formed, whereas in condensation polymerisation a **..........** molecule is also produced at each linkage.
cards.back_md: In addition polymerisation, **one** product is formed, whereas in condensation polymerisation a **water** molecule is also produced at each linkage.

front_blocks.md: What two functional groups are present in the monomers used to make nylon?

back_blocks.md: The monomers used to make nylon each carry a **-COOH** (carboxylic acid) group and an **-NH**<sub>**2**</sub> (amine) group. These groups react to form amide linkages.

cards.front_md: What two functional groups are present in the monomers used to make nylon?
cards.back_md: The monomers used to make nylon each carry a **-COOH** (carboxylic acid) group and an **-NH**<sub>**2**</sub> (amine) group. These groups react to form amide linkages.

front_blocks.md: Nylon is an addition polymer made from alkene monomers.

back_blocks.md: Nylon is a **condensation polymer** (a polyamide) made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine, not from alkene monomers.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Nylon is an addition polymer made from alkene monomers.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Nylon is a **condensation polymer** (a polyamide) made from a dicarboxylic acid and a diamine, not from alkene monomers.

front_blocks.md: How do you deduce the monomer of an addition polymer from its repeat unit?

back_blocks.md: To deduce the monomer, identify the repeat unit, then change the single bond in the repeat unit back to a **C=C double bond** and remove the continuation bonds at each end.

cards.front_md: How do you deduce the monomer of an addition polymer from its repeat unit?
cards.back_md: To deduce the monomer, identify the repeat unit, then change the single bond in the repeat unit back to a **C=C double bond** and remove the continuation bonds at each end.

front_blocks.md: Nylon is classified as a poly**..........** because it contains amide linkages formed between -COOH and -NH<sub>2</sub> groups.

back_blocks.md: Nylon is classified as a poly**amide** because it contains amide linkages formed between -COOH and -NH<sub>2</sub> groups.

cards.back_md: Nylon is classified as a poly**amide** because it contains amide linkages formed between -COOH and -NH<sub>2</sub> groups.

front_blocks.md: What is the key difference between the monomers used in addition polymerisation and those used in condensation polymerisation?

back_blocks.md: Addition polymerisation uses alkene monomers containing a **C=C double bond** (one type of monomer).
Condensation polymerisation uses two different monomers, each with **two functional groups**, one at each end.
